gaps.name: Unread-reaction badge and jump-to-next-reaction in chat
gaps.whatItIs: Modern chat shows a floating circular badge above the scroll-down button with the count of reactions you have not seen, tapping it jumps to the next reacted message and marks it read.
gaps.whyItMatters: In a busy group a reaction to your own message is currently invisible unless you happen to scroll past it; there is no way to find who reacted to you.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m, next to the existing scroll-to-bottom control; TGClient+Reactions.h already has -unreadReactionsInChat:fromMessageId:limit:completion: and -markReactionsReadInChat:, neither is called from any .m outside the category.

gaps.name: Unread reaction / mention counters on chat list rows
gaps.whatItIs: The chat list draws a separate small badge for unread mentions and unread reactions beside the unread-message count.
gaps.whyItMatters: Without it a user cannot tell from the list which chat contains a reaction aimed at them; the reaction feature is effectively write-only for the receiver.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGChatListViewController.m row drawing and the chat dictionary built in TGClient+ChatList.m — grep shows no unread_reaction_count / unread_mention_count is even read out of the TDLib chat object there, although TGTopicsViewController.m already renders the same counter for forum topics.
tdlib: chat.unread_reaction_count / unread_mention_count from the chat object (not currently mapped in TGClient+ChatList.m)

gaps.name: Choosing the quick (double-tap) reaction
gaps.whatItIs: Settings holds a default reaction the double-tap gesture sends; the modern client lets you pick it from the reaction grid.
gaps.whyItMatters: We ship the double-tap gesture and TGReactionPickerView.m reads -quickReactionEmoji, but -setQuickReactionEmoji: is never called from any screen, so every user is permanently stuck on the thumbs-up default.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGSettingsViewController.m, a row that opens a small emoji grid built from -activeReactionsWithCompletion: (same grid the picker strip already builds in TGReactionPickerView.m).

gaps.name: Reaction notification settings row
gaps.whatItIs: Notifications settings has a Reactions section: notify from everyone / contacts only / nobody, plus preview and sound, for message reactions and story reactions.
gaps.whyItMatters: In any group of size, reaction notifications are the noisiest source of pushes and there is currently no way to turn them down.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGSettingsViewController.m notifications section; -setReactionNotificationSource:showPreview:soundId: exists in TGClient+Reactions.h and is called from nowhere.
tdlib: reactionNotificationSettings update is not routed — the screen must hold local state, as the header already notes

gaps.name: Admin screen for which reactions a chat allows
gaps.whatItIs: PeerAllowedReactionsScreen: an admin picks All / Some / None and, for Some, ticks the individual emoji, plus the max reactions per message for channels.
gaps.whyItMatters: Group and channel owners cannot switch reactions off or restrict them from this client at all, which is a routine moderation action.
gaps.whereItGoes: A Reactions row in the group/channel admin area of TGProfileViewController.m (which already lists reactToMessages permission text at line 1924); -setAvailableReactionsInChat:emojis:maxCount: is wrapped and unused. Modern reference: submodules/TelegramUI/Components/PeerAllowedReactionsScreen.

gaps.name: Per-emoji tabs in the who-reacted list
gaps.whatItIs: ReactionListContextMenuContent puts a header of tabs across the reader list — All, then one tab per emoji with its count — so you can see just who sent a specific reaction, paged as you scroll.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGReactionPickerView.m fetches the reader list unfiltered (line ~1148); on a post with five different reactions the list is an undifferentiated scroll and you cannot answer "who disliked this".
gaps.whereItGoes: The reader list already inside TGReactionPickerView.m — add a segmented header and pass the emoji filter argument that -addedReactionsForMessage:inChat:emoji:offset:limit:completion: already accepts.
tdlib: getMessageAddedReactions with reaction_type filter (wrapped, emoji argument currently always nil)

gaps.name: Paid (star) reactions on channel posts
gaps.whatItIs: A star chip on channel posts: tap to add one star reaction, a slider to send many at once, a few seconds of Undo before it commits, a top-senders strip, and a toggle to send anonymously or as a chat.
gaps.whyItMatters: Catalogued as blocked, but the block is wrong: StoreKit only prevents *buying* stars, and TGClient+Payments.h already wraps the whole spend path (-addPaidReactionToMessage:, -commitPaidReactionsOnMessage:, -cancelPaidReactionsOnMessage:, -setPaidReactionAnonymous:, -paidReactionSendersInChat:) and we already ship TGStarsViewController. A user with a star balance simply cannot spend it on posts, and cannot even see that a post has paid reactions — TGClient+Reactions.h renders paid reactions as a placeholder star glyph with no interaction.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGReactionPickerView.m chip row (a distinct star chip) plus a small sheet reusing the existing TGSnackbar undo banner for the commit timer; balance and top-up live in TGStarsViewController.m.

gaps.name: Displaying custom-emoji reactions as static images
gaps.whatItIs: Premium users react with arbitrary custom emoji; every client, premium or not, renders those chips as the emoji's image.
gaps.whyItMatters: Catalogued blocked, and *sending* genuinely is (premium plus animated formats), but *showing* is not: today TGClient+Reactions.h substitutes a star character, so a post reacted to entirely with custom emoji shows a row of identical meaningless stars with counts. We already decode static WebP sticker thumbnails through UIImage+WebP.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGReactionChipsView in TGReactionPickerView.m, fetching the sticker for the custom_emoji_id through the existing TGClient+Stickers / TGClient+Files download path.

gaps.name: Reaction chip state driven by updates instead of polling
gaps.whatItIs: Modern clients update chips from updateMessageInteractionInfo pushed by the server, instantly and at zero cost.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGClient+Reactions.h states the watcher polls -reactionChipsForMessage: on a 5s timer, one request per watched message. On a 4S with several visible reacted messages that is a steady stream of requests and wakeups purely to observe something the server already pushes — it costs battery and makes chips lag by up to five seconds.
gaps.whereItGoes: Route updateMessageInteractionInfo in TGClient.m's update dispatch and have the watch table in TGClient+Reactions.m consume it, keeping the timer only as a fallback.
tdlib: updateDefaultReactionType, updateReactionNotificationSettings (also unrouted — would remove the two 'we cache it locally' caveats in the header)
